newsitem.title: UK: Brent gains in paper market, spreads firm.
newsitem.headline: Brent gains in paper market, spreads firm.

text.p: Brent gained on a quiet paper market on Friday with intermonth spreads steady to slightly up and contracts for differences mixed, traders said.
No physical trades were reported on the North Sea market early on Friday but a European major said it bought a May 20 cargo of Beryl on Thursday but the price was undisclosed.
Three Brent cargoes were due to turn wet on Friday.
Traders said most North Sea grades seemed to be steady with the exception of Oseberg, which was suffering from excess availability.
One European buyer said he believed there were more than 15 May cargoes of the Norwegian sweet crude still unsold.
In the cash market, June Brent was trading eight cents up at $18.37 by 1159 GMT.
No paper trades were reported but Brent intermonth spreads were steady or slightly firmer.

May/June was hardly changed at -22/-18 cents in thin talk after being set at -23/-18 cents in late U.S. talk while June/July tightened four cents, talked at about -9 cents after being traded at -13 cents in late U.S. trade.
July/Aug was one cent firmer at about -11/-8 cents from -12/-10 cents.

Brent CFDs were mixed. May 5-9 firmed three cents to talk June Brent -30 cts and the week after was steady at June Brent -32/-31 cents. But May 19-23 was talked three cents weaker than Wednesday's levels.
Mediterranean and West African markets remained fairly quiet with prices holding steady.

Traders said lighter West African grades were well supported by Far Eastern and transatlantic demand while prices for distillate rich Forcados, though seasonally out of favour, were underpinned by demand into the Mediterranean for its diesel properties.
They said buying for June FOB barrels was becoming the focus of interest with May cargoes mostly tied up.
"The market should stay pretty firm in the near term but we May see the usual price volatility when NNPC starts pricing for June," one trader said.
Forcados was valued steady around dated Brent +10 cents a barrel while Bonny light was valued around dated Brent +47 cents after a May 25-27 loading cargo was traded on Thursday.
In a very quiet Mediterranean market prices for Russian Urals crude were holding steady around dated Brent -$1/-90 cents.
